title.en: Graphic shape language across asset types

summary: Define a small grammar of masses, cuts, edges and exceptions, then translate its relationships into unlike objects without forcing them into one silhouette.
objective: A character and a shelter, or a product and an environment module, read as one authored world while each remains identifiable and functional.
applies_when: Several unlike asset families need a shared visual identity.
A named style is already chosen but its geometry decisions are inconsistent across objects.
intent_signals: make a character and building feel from the same world
translate a graphic motif across unlike assets
example_prompts: Give a courier character and a transit shelter the same cut-corner and suspended-gap language while keeping the doorway and limbs functional.
negative_signals: Copying one outline onto every asset.
Calling a palette alone a shape language.
not_for: A historical definition of a named visual movement.
A mechanical interface or clearance specification.

principles: Write the grammar as relationships: which masses dominate, how curves meet flats, where gaps open, and which functional parts may break the pattern. Do not prescribe a universal count or ratio.
Translate a motif by role. A cut corner on a handheld tool can become a roof return or a character cuff; literal repetition is optional.
Keep one declared exception class for identity, function or focal emphasis so consistency does not erase subject meaning.
implementation: Build a two-column Blender proof with unlike objects at the same intended screen scale. Block primary masses first; use named bevel, taper, inset and negative-space decisions before surface detail.

Mark motif roles in object/material names or review notes. Export final geometry, normals and material slots through glTF; treat Grease Pencil strokes, compositor outlines and non-exported procedural effects as authored source that needs baked texture, mesh representation or an explicitly rebuilt Three.js effect.

In Three.js, preserve object identity and motif roles while choosing screen-space outline/detail thresholds per camera. Do not let responsive simplification remove a functional opening, grasp point or selection boundary.
observable_checks: At thumbnail scale, identify each subject and point to at least two shared relationships without relying on color.
Rotate both objects to a second required view: the grammar still appears, but doors, limbs, handles and mating edges remain plausible.
Disable runtime outlines and post effects: transported geometry still carries the declared primary shape language; any missing authored effect is listed as a runtime owner.

creative_affordances: Use rounded slabs, blade-like tapers, scalloped voids or asymmetrical interruptions; the record chooses a translation method, not an aesthetic.
Let a focal object deliberately break one relationship when the brief needs contrast.
known_limits: Authored creative proposal; it does not prove aesthetic preference, historical authenticity or functional engineering.
No Blender export or Three.js view was run.
